question: Pohár medu v špajzi po pár mesiacoch zhustne a zbelie. Čo sa s ním v skutočnosti stalo?
source_excerpt: Honey crystallizes because glucose separates from water in a supersaturated solution, forming solid crystals that change texture but do not spoil it.

extra.why_interesting: Almost every Slovak household has a jar of honey that has gone thick and white in the pantry. Many people assume it went bad or was adulterated with sugar. The answer reassures them: crystallization is natural and often a sign of real honey.
extra.verification_notes: Honey that thickens and whitens has crystallized (glucose separating from water), a physical change and not spoilage; see https://savannahbee.com/blogs/honey-education-hub/why-honey-crystallizes

explanation: Med je presýtený roztok cukrov a glukóza z neho postupne vypadáva v podobe drobných kryštálikov. Nie je pokazený ani falšovaný, stačí ho jemne zohriať vo vodnom kúpeli do 40 °C a znova bude tekutý.

question: Kliešťovú encefalitídu môžete na Slovensku chytiť aj bez toho, aby vás kliešť vôbec uhryzol. Cez akú potravinu?
source_excerpt: konzumáciou nedostatočne tepelne upraveného mlieka a mliečnych ovčích či kozích výrobkov infikovaných zvierat. Slovensko má najviac potravinových epidémií kliešťovej encefalitídy v Európe.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone in Slovakia knows ticks spread encephalitis and checks themselves after a walk in the woods. Few realize the same disease can come from a glass of fresh farm milk, a very Slovak risk tied to sheep and goat farming and home-made cheeses.
extra.verification_notes: NCZI confirms TBE spreads via insufficiently heat-treated milk and sheep/goat dairy products in Slovakia, so raw milk is a valid answer.

explanation: Kliešť nakazí kozu, ovcu alebo kravu a vírus potom prechádza do jej mlieka. Slovensko patrí k európskym krajinám s najčastejšími nákazami z čerstvého kozieho či ovčieho mlieka a syrov z neho.
